value: males chose the 650 nm LED most often, significantly more than the other colours; selection of 520 nm, 580 nm and the white control (CK) did not differ significantly
method: behavioural: choice of an LED stimulus in a darkroom hexagonal maze, males, six stimuli (380, 440, 520, 580, 650 nm, white CK)
conditions: Beetles tested in a darkroom in a black-cardboard hexagonal maze (base edge 20 cm); a light was scored as preferred if the adult stayed in its arena room more than 1 min; 100 males and 100 females tested separately, 10 beetles per run, 3 replicates. Six stimuli: LEDs of 380, 440, 520, 580 and 650 nm plus a white control (CK). Stimulus intensity was not matched: illuminance (lux, a human-weighted measure that does not equate quanta at 380 nm or 650 nm) was 1400 lx at 380 nm, 2360 at 440, 2100 at 520, 2430 at 580, 600 at 650 and 4500 for white (Table 1, tool reading), so the most-chosen 650 nm stimulus was the dimmest by this measure; no sentence in the paper states the intensities were equal. Percentages appear only in Figure 3. The wavelength-preference test shows what beetles chose, and does not separate colour discrimination from phototaxis to brightness in a spectral band. The omitted middle of the sentence gives the test statistic, F5,12 = 19.96, p < 0.001, and the lowest male rates as 380 nm and 440 nm.

value: green LED trap (peak about 521-524 nm) caught the highest share of released wasps among six LED colours: 67% recaptured, significantly higher than all other colours (p = 0.0001)
method: behavioural: 24 h multiple-choice cage assay, parasitoids released and recaptured on sticky traps carrying UV, blue, cyan, green, yellow and red LEDs
conditions: Climate chamber 25 +/- 1 C, 18 h light:6 h dark; 40 wasps released per run from 0.7 m; two cages (0.8 x 1 x 1 m) used at once; 20 replicates with the cage as unit. LED colour had a significant effect on mean recapture (F = 94.7, df = 5, p = 0.001); 61% of all released wasps were recaptured on the six traps. Every LED trap except UV was adjusted to equal photon flux, 8.1 umol m-2 s-1; UV was measured with a UV-A sensor and converted to photon flux density but not adjusted, and the paper gives no reason (tool reading). Recapture on a sticky trap records arrival and landing, so it combines colour choice with attraction to light; the parasitoid's spectral sensitivity was not measured.

method: behavioural: 24 h multiple-choice cage assay, parasitoids released and recaptured on sticky traps carrying UV, blue, cyan, green, yellow and red LEDs
conditions: Same assay as the green-LED record. The UV trap, whose intensity was measured and converted but not adjusted to the 8.1 umol m-2 s-1 of the other traps, caught significantly fewer wasps than the other colours (17%, p = 0.0026), and green caught 67%. Blue, red, cyan and yellow therefore sit together below green and above UV. Equal photon flux does not equalise how bright the colours look to a wasp, whose receptor classes were not measured here.
